feedback: Iteration 3 (0.6 kg, otherwise the iteration-2 geometry) is the best race so far at 575.8, up from 501.2. The oval still completes 20 of 20, and the s-bend completion held at 12 of 20, so the mass change did not hurt the s-bend. The slalom still fails 20 of 20, with max_error 0.0645 m and progress 0.1975. Its line losses are 1.0 per run, so the spread of +/-0.024 m is not limiting. Oval oscillation stayed at 0.21, so yaw inertia alone did not cut it. This suggests the controller's damping and steady bias matter too, so I am changing controller terms this iteration and holding your geometry. Expected, not measured: your hypothesis that slalom max_error stays near 0.06 m with line losses at or below 2 per run looks consistent with the data so far. For the next geometry, if the slalom max_error is still at or above 0.06 m with line losses at or below 2 per run after this race, the forward offset y = 0.07 m (spread unchanged) is the next lever, as you planned. If slalom line losses rise above about 2 per run with progress below 0.2, widen the spread to x = +/-0.032 m. If s-bend completion drops below 0.3, revert mass to 0.8 kg, since the 0.6 kg result is only a small improvement and the s-bend is the track most sensitive to it.
requested_changes: Hold the geometry as iteration 3 (five sensors at y = 0.06 m, x = +/-0.024 m, 12 mm footprint, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.6 kg) and test y = 0.07 m next only if the slalom max_error is still at or above 0.06 m with line losses at or below 2 per run.
If slalom line_loss_events rise above about 2 per run with slalom progress below 0.2, widen the spread to x = +/-0.032 m with five sensors and keep y as it is.
If s-bend completion falls below 0.3 at 0.6 kg, revert mass to 0.8 kg before adding spread, because the s-bend completed most often under the 0.8 kg design.
